channel.title: Unown blog
channel.description: How each feature and release works, what it does, and the receipts behind it — the longhand record of the self-improving terminal coding agent Unown.

item.title: The memory-engine round: dream-now that dreamed nothing
item.description: Every write lane, dream, read lane and tier combination driven live against a real engine — a dream button that lied, a search lane that whispered empty.

item.title: The combination round 2: the approval option that never asked
item.description: The second pass over every plan-mode × TUI combination found an approval option whose promise was silent vapor — and a boot lane still dropping its flags.

item.title: The combination round: the flag that never worked, and the gate that wouldn't stay closed
item.description: A full pass over every plan-mode combination found a flagship flag that silently did nothing, an approval gate that re-opened while you typed, and more.

item.title: Ostinato: the round where the hardening came first
item.description: The repo's second user product - a keyboard-first, offline-first spaced-repetition PWA shipped under a harden-first programme, with receipts.

item.title: The spend-and-memory-health round: two honest misses become two honest cards
item.description: The settings benchmark's two pinned search misses both flip — automation spend gets a meter and ceilings, memory gets a health card.

item.title: Coda: the round where unown shipped its first user product
item.description: The Coda round shipped the repo's first installable app - a local-first markdown notes and task-board PWA built entirely by agent tickets.

item.title: The doc-truth round: the maintenance pass that made every documented number true
item.description: The doc-truth round re-derived and corrected every drifted count, measured the Coda PWA null with a receipt, and priced the instruction-surface PR lane.

item.title: The hints-ranking round: when six new facts shouldn't evict the one that matters
item.description: The browser-memory hint digest becomes category-balanced — round-robin across idiom classes so a burst of new facts cannot evict the dialog lesson.

item.title: The browser autonomy round: dogfooding the browser until it taught us back
item.description: One hostile checkout page, five blind runs, two real defects found and fixed in-round, and the first receipts of a browser tool that remembers what broke.

item.title: Round 2: when the browser remembered before it clicked
item.description: Closing the recall-vs-application gap — a tool-time memory hint lane, and the run where the agent armed the dialog before the trap.

item.title: Six updates, one pixel diff: shipping a dependency round you can trust
item.description: How Unown updates packages without regressions: staged gates, an A/B pixel diff of the landing page, and the word budget the changelog almost broke.

item.title: The release that never was: re-cutting v0.0.53 from a red tag
item.description: The tag shipped while CI was red on all three OSes, so the release never published. The story of the one-way latch that caused it — and the fix.

item.title: Four alerts, three findings, zero regressions: the security round
item.description: How Unown cleared every open Dependabot advisory and CodeQL finding in one gated round — including the one Dependabot's own patch would have left broken.

item.title: The footer quiet round: what a terminal owes you at rest
item.description: The area below the input showed four rows of chrome before you typed a word. This round made it two — and made every chip earn its row.

item.title: The keyboard round: the shortcut that never worked, and five more finds
item.description: The planning round's headline shortcut never worked on a fresh install. The keyboard round found it and five more, fixed all six, verified live.

item.title: Plan Mode V2: the round where unown learned to actually plan
item.description: A scored plan file, an approval gate, and two mechanical convergence lanes took plan mode from zero plans produced to 100/100 — with receipts.

item.title: The sessions round: abort and resume, made consistent
item.description: One abort matrix behind Esc, /abort and every protocol; both session stores behind every picker; resume in both grammars the field ships.

item.title: The settings round: when your diff view lies to every fresh install
item.description: Minting the round's authoring failures into guards found three real defects — including a diff view that lied on every fresh install. Measured and pinned.

item.title: The todo unification round: why you saw two to-do lists in plan mode
item.description: The plan-steps widget and the seeded Todos panel both mounted after approval. This round made them one list — verified live, with receipts.

item.title: The craft axes: teaching the agent to see what elite pages never do
item.description: The second Website Excellence round: nine elite sites from production CSS, six new enforceable critique gates, and the app that passed on iteration three.

item.title: The delegation round: every spawn now says why
item.description: Unown 0.0.46: the why field, the delegation audit ledger, four specialist agents, and a measured 76→79 with the runaway-scout shape dead — receipts inside.

item.title: The model-specs round: never guess a context window again
item.description: Unown 0.0.47: specs detected from verifiable sources, asked for when nothing knows, provenance everywhere, and a bridge that learns limits from upstream 400s.

item.title: The observability round: can you read your agent's state in 60 seconds?
item.description: A mission panel, a 60-second brief, a recovery card, receipts-only confidence and an ambient learning feed — the round the terminal learned to explain itself.

item.title: The PLM round: unown now tracks itself as processes
item.description: A 12-state machine for every engine activity, governed tool invocations, a recovery ledger — and the machine caught its own wiring bugs live.

item.title: The provider round: what nine competitors taught unown about connecting a model
item.description: Wire-aware probes, a rate-limit verdict that stops lying, masked key entry everywhere, and latency chips — the 2026-10-30 hardening of the provider path.

item.title: The encore round: an agent that critiqued its own design work, then beat its own gates
item.description: The gallery's eighth app, built inside a measured design loop — every screenshot scored, every failure ledgered, every number traced to a receipt.

item.title: The nocturne round: the agent built an incident-ops platform — and got better building it
item.description: Gallery app #7 — Nocturne, a multi-tenant incident-ops platform: 28 sessions, 473 tests, a 10/10 live browser pass, six failures pinned.

item.title: The SOTA round: Fugue, and the loop that watched it build
item.description: The fifth gallery app, built by unown while the loop minted skills, dreamed, and published an honest null — the receipts behind the showcase band.

item.title: The validation round: cold-starting the learning loop, then pointing it at itself
item.description: A fresh clone, an empty engine DB, one tracked memory file — a validation programme that found drift, poisoning, and a dead-ended mint, then fixed all three.

item.title: The cadence round: a habit tracker, a real bug in unown, and a three-app gallery
item.description: One round, every SDLC stage: planned, built, browser-QA'd, reviewed twice — and the review caught a TDZ crash in unown itself. Three apps live.

item.title: The carving round: the letters draw themselves
item.description: Glyph draw-on for the decode panel and the spellbox, a decode fill that stays AA at every frame, keycap chips, and copy buttons that finally speak.

item.title: The commerce round: a storefront, a checkout, and a browser QA pass
item.description: Three SDLC rounds — planned, reviewed, browser-QA'd — and the landing page now frames two agent-built apps in a live gallery: 838 calls, one SHIP verdict.

item.title: The live preview round: the landing page now runs what the agent built
item.description: Four sessions, ~200 tool calls, one fullstack app — and the landing page now runs it instead of showing a video. The category's first live agent-built demo.

item.title: The parley round: a multi-tenant SaaS, two P0s found by the adversarial review
item.description: The gallery's fourth app adds tenancy, real auth, RBAC and isolation — and the round's failures became pinned regressions and agent skills.

item.title: The presence round: six effects that make the landing page answer you
item.description: A decode wave, a scroll route bar, a nav that names your band, pointer spotlights and counted receipts — additive effects, finished base states.

item.title: The builder round: one prompt, a whole app, filmed end to end
item.description: One prompt into an empty directory; 47 tool calls later a full-stack app with a green 39-test suite and a live-verified API. The whole build, on film.

item.title: The long-run round: what breaks when the agent works for hours
item.description: Eleven endurance scenarios, 150-turn buildouts, forced compaction and kill-resume torture — five layered defects fixed, ten more in the runner itself.

item.title: The security round: every open advisory, closed at the source
item.description: Eleven Dependabot alerts, three CodeQL findings, one lockfile incident — the advisory surface went to zero by fixing causes, not findings.

item.title: The chaos round: orphaned fleets, stolen steering, and the reports that lied
item.description: The chaos round: nested CLI calls, watchdog kills, oversized reports, slow children outliving the process. Seven findings, fixed and pinned.

item.title: The hardening round: the verdict on the detached engine
item.description: We re-litigated the core USP's architecture against ten competitor repos and 54 sources. The detached engine stays; six honest-failure lanes ship in v0.0.28.

item.title: The ledger round: the seams the chaos round wrote down
item.description: Round three paid the chaos round's IOUs: the stop that couldn't un-park, the re-ask that vanished, the name with no entropy, the crash with no trace.

item.title: The orphan round: the lane with no ledger of its own
item.description: Round four paid the ledger's last IOU: the sync lane's kill -9 orphans — alive, unrecorded, swept by nobody — now journal, heartbeat, and sweep.

item.title: The SOTA memory-eval round: four suites, one real fix, and a bill paid
item.description: How our memory system earned its numbers: gold-op ledgers, dual-embedder retrieval, a calibrated judge, twelve failure modes — and the bug they caught.

item.title: The SOTA re-cut: thirteen reels re-filmed, and how we audit demo video
item.description: A frame-sampled VLM audit sent thirteen landing reels back into the capture harness — and the first audit pass itself was wrong about what it saw.

item.title: The stress round: what breaks when a real user drives the browser
item.description: Fifteen hostile scenarios and seven competitor repos exposed three browser-agent architecture bugs — all closed in v0.0.29.

item.title: The subagent stress round: what a real model found that the scripted tests could not
item.description: Ten live scenarios drove the subagent stack the way its docs promise — six real defects found, two of them silently broken features, all fixed and pinned.

item.title: The memory that proves itself before it ships
item.description: How Unown turns session notes into four-tier project memory, why the files stay plain markdown, and what the engine verifies before keeping any of it.

item.title: Unown is in beta — here is what that means
item.description: The self-improving terminal coding agent is in beta: what works, what moves, and where to report what breaks while the 0.0.x line grows up.

item.title: v0.0.15 — every capability filmed, the atlas passes review
item.description: The media-completion and sprite-craft round: the dex ships 24 movies on 22 entries with zero pending plates, and the creature atlas passes its review lane.
